meta.title: Primordial Paradox pacing, text and cutscene recipes
meta.citation_note: Recipes carry source ids only. Every id resolves to a title, a link and a read date in section 10 of the study, never here, because this directory is scanned by tools/check_cleanroom.py and that gate refuses several game names as whole words anywhere under data/. Do not paste a source URL into this file.
meta.reference_rule: study only, measured in words and numbers; no asset, text, layout, notation or code was copied, ripped, traced or decompiled

units.distance: tiles of 16 by 16 pixels, and metres for real places
units.screen: 16 by 15 tiles visible in a 256 by 240 frame

meta.sources_block: see the study, section 10, ids P-01 to P-23

recipes.name: Title to first input
recipes.when_to_use: Every cold boot. This is the whole budget between power on and the player pressing anything.
forbidden: a logo that needs more than 3 seconds to read at 256 by 240
a publisher or engine splash between the logo and PRESS START
a blink faster than 30 steps on and off, which reads as a fault rather than a prompt

recipes.name: Cold boot to PRESS START
recipes.when_to_use: Building the boot path and the first scene.
forbidden: a black screen longer than 2 seconds on a machine with no loading to hide
any text before the logo other than the licence and publisher line

recipes.name: Intro crawl length
recipes.when_to_use: Writing or editing data/intro_text.json.
forbidden: a crawl over 25 seconds, which is longer than the drive's shortest three shots together
more than 4 lines in one beat at 32 columns
moving the crop of the crawl upward: our crawl reveals line by line in place, it does not scroll like a chapter card

recipes.name: Crawl typing speed and beat pauses
recipes.when_to_use: The crawl runner, and any other full screen text that is not the dialogue box.
forbidden: the box's 2 steps a character here: 30 characters a second across 32 columns reads as a glitch at full screen
an auto advance that cuts off the last line of a beat

recipes.name: Skip guard on the crawl
recipes.when_to_use: Any story text the player has already seen once, and the first view too, because a lost first view is unforgivable and a forced second view is worse.

params.skips_to: the next gameplay scene, not a chapter card

forbidden: a single tap skipping the story, because a double tap on START during the fade would take it
a skip that lands on a black screen
a skip available during beat 1

recipes.name: Idle attract loop
recipes.when_to_use: The title when the player walks away, and every demo kiosk build.
forbidden: an attract loop that shows content the player has not reached, beyond the first two minutes
a loop that resets the save file list

recipes.name: Dialogue box type speed
recipes.when_to_use: Every page in the box, from the first caption in the car to the last line of the ending.
forbidden: a text speed setting in a menu the player must find, which was the shipped patch for a slow battle message in the reference JRPG
fast forward that skips a whole page
two advances from one press

recipes.name: Punctuation pauses
recipes.when_to_use: The typewriter loop.
forbidden: a pause longer than 30 steps inside a page, which belongs to a cutscene command rather than punctuation
any fade or blink in the middle of a page

recipes.name: Page geometry and page cycle
recipes.when_to_use: Sizing every dialogue page and estimating a scene's cost against the beat sheet.
forbidden: a page of one line when two lines fit, because the press costs the same
text that overflows the box; the checker refuses it, the runtime never truncates

recipes.name: Dialogue budget per scene
recipes.when_to_use: Authoring any cutscene or conversation, and reviewing one that feels long.
forbidden: a scene over 12 pages, which should be two scenes
a page that exists only to explain what the previous page explained

recipes.name: Text speed benchmark table
recipes.when_to_use: Any argument about whether our text is too fast or too slow. Quote this table instead of an opinion.
forbidden: citing a frames a character figure for a game that shipped a bare 1 to 8 slider, because the two are not convertible

recipes.name: Cutscene shot length
recipes.when_to_use: Boarding out a scene, especially the drive.
forbidden: a shot under 6 seconds on a 256 by 240 screen
two shots of the same composition back to back
a hard cut that does not land on a musical downbeat

recipes.name: Fade lengths
recipes.when_to_use: Every scene change and act boundary.
forbidden: a fade longer than 24 steps, which reads as a loading pause
a fade out and fade in with no frame held between them

recipes.name: Camera move
recipes.when_to_use: Any scripted pan, and the intro's only camera led shot.
forbidden: a camera move behind an open text box
more than 3 moves in one beat, which makes the beat about the camera
an eased or interpolated move: the move is linear and floored to whole pixels

recipes.name: Music as the clock
recipes.when_to_use: Placing every music change in a cutscene.
forbidden: a music change in the middle of a page of text
a cue that starts under the fade in and is replaced before the fade ends

recipes.name: Lightning flash and screen shake
recipes.when_to_use: The storm that follows the car, and every impact that needs weight without a cut.

params.flash_palette: the NES flash palette already used on the title

forbidden: a flash longer than 2 frames, which is a strobe and a health risk
more than one flash every 2 seconds
shake on a text box

recipes.name: No car interior
recipes.when_to_use: Every beat that happens while the car is moving. This is Nayil's decision of 2026-10-21 and it is not a style preference.

params.dialogue_device: radio, captions at the bottom of the frame, the car in long shot

forbidden: a windscreen view from inside
a rear view mirror shot
a portrait or face in the car
any HUD readable inside the car

recipes.name: The screen as the unit of map
recipes.when_to_use: Sizing any map, and comparing our areas with the NES reference rooms.
forbidden: quoting a map size in tiles when talking to Nayil, who reads maps in screens
a screen with fewer than 3 interactables or none, at any point in the first hour

recipes.name: First area size and first reward
recipes.when_to_use: Laying out the dock yard, which is the first place the player walks.

params.reference_first_area: one room and one cave, reward in under a minute

forbidden: an opening area larger than 12 screens
a first reward that is money rather than capability

recipes.name: First hub size
recipes.when_to_use: The dock office and the ship's public rooms.
forbidden: a hub with one door and five facades
a shop that opens before the first fight

recipes.name: Interest density along a route
recipes.when_to_use: Every route between two places a player must walk.
forbidden: two consecutive screens with nothing to press
an interactable placed on a screen the player can only cross once

recipes.name: Screen crossing time
recipes.when_to_use: Converting any walk into seconds when filling a beat sheet.
forbidden: budgeting a cutscene by walking time alone, because ten screens is only 32 seconds
a walk longer than 4 screens with no text and no encounter

recipes.name: Encounter model, and why the reference roll is refused
recipes.when_to_use: Any proposal to add random encounters, and any argument about encounter frequency.

params.our_model: visible markers, touched to start a battle

forbidden: a per tile roll at our walking speed, which would be a fight every 1.6 to 4.8 seconds
citing the reference rates as a target rather than as a ceiling

recipes.name: Marker density
recipes.when_to_use: Placing encounter markers on any outdoor map.
forbidden: a marker every 8 tiles, which is the reference's most generous terrain and still too often here
a marker placed where the player cannot see it before touching it

recipes.name: Encounter and trigger grace
recipes.when_to_use: Every map entry, door, and the tile where a cutscene hands control back.
forbidden: a fight in the first second of control
a door tile that re-fires its own scene on the way out

recipes.name: Battle length by kind
recipes.when_to_use: Balancing any fight that appears in the first hour, and judging a boss that feels long.
forbidden: a first fight that can be lost
a field fight over 60 seconds before the third area
a boss over 150 seconds with no phase change

recipes.name: Save spacing
recipes.when_to_use: Any stretch of dangerous walking, and the first save point in the opening.

params.autosave_on: entering a new map, after the fade in

forbidden: a save point behind a wall the player has to find
an autosave during a battle or a cutscene
more than 12 screens between saves on a route with markers

recipes.name: Save models in the reference set
recipes.when_to_use: Deciding what a save point looks like in the fiction, and writing its one page of text.

params.zelda: the death prompt, then continue, losing the room and not the run
params.first_jrpg: talk to the king in the first castle
params.mother_style: pick up any telephone and call the father
params.indie_2015: star points, the first one a room after the rescue, free and healing nothing
params.ours: the ship's log terminal, plus autosave on map entry

forbidden: a save point with a menu of its own
a save prompt that costs more than one page

recipes.name: Tile to metres for real places
recipes.when_to_use: Any map drafted from OpenStreetMap, and any claim of the form this is really that street.
forbidden: a tile smaller than 4 m, because a street then cannot fit a car and two pavements
reusing an OSM draft without the ODbL attribution line

recipes.name: Drive compression
recipes.when_to_use: Boarding out any journey that is real road, and defending the number of shots it gets.
forbidden: fewer than 6 distinct locations for a journey over 60 minutes
a compression ratio better than 40 to 1, which stops being a journey and becomes a slideshow
two shots of the same road type in a row

recipes.name: City map compression
recipes.when_to_use: Any walk in a real town, including Southampton Town Quay and Winchester High Street.
forbidden: mapping a whole town at 8 m a tile, which is 11 screens of walking for a street two minutes long in life
a real landmark placed at the wrong end of the street, because the real order is the one thing the draft gives for free

recipes.name: The fifteen minute gates
recipes.when_to_use: Any change to the opening, and the review question when the first fifteen minutes is re-cut.
forbidden: a first input later than 2 min 30 s, which every reference opening in the study beats
a cutscene share over 60 percent in the first fifteen minutes
a first save later than the tenth minute

beat_sheet.title: Primordial Paradox, first fifteen minutes, proposed 2026-10-22

beats.beat: Title attract: logo, moon, storm cloud, one lightning flash, loops until START
PRESS START, menu, NEW GAME confirmed
Fade to black, star field, sickle and bolt constellations
Crawl beats 1 to 2, the gods forgotten
Crawl beats 3 to 4, the four who do not know
Crawl beats 5 to 6, entropy, Southampton, October, and hold
Fade in on Big Ben at night, camera pans down to the street
London street, the car pulls away, the Thames
M3 gantry with the Southampton distance sign
Rain starts, wipers seen from outside the car
Radio, four caption pages, no portrait, car in long shot
Winchester services, the player walks one screen and reads a sign (first input)
Twyford Down cutting at night, headlight pool on chalk
Winchester Cathedral silhouette far off, one caption
Radio, three caption pages, the subject turns to the sea
Storm cloud over the car, first lightning, 2 frame palette flash
Chalk downland, moon, road markers, the storm keeping pace
Hard cut to the slip road, Southampton sign, headlights
The docks, cranes, containers, the ship lit at the quay
Gate checkpoint, guard, four pages, one three option choice
Full control, the dock yard, 3 screens, no text
Dock office, two people, six pages, the boarding pass
First encounter marker, the hold hound, one command win
Quay side walk, 2 screens, one short caption about the water
Gangway, deck, the ship's horn, the door
Ship corridor, 3 rooms, free walk
Cabin, the ship's log, first save, two pages and the menu
Second encounter in the hold, teaches TALK, cannot be lost
Stairwell and upper deck, free walk
The ship leaves port, the Quay receding, no text
Kronos seen from the deck, sickle of stars, no text
Chapter card and fade to black

checks.unused_note: P-10 and P-11 are the reference JRPG world map measurements, cited in the study section 5 table and not needed by a recipe parameter; P-17 and P-23 are background and the local spec set.
